name: Quickwit
tagline: Cloud-native search engine on object storage for logs and traces, built on Tantivy.
description: Quickwit is a Rust search engine designed for append-only observability data: logs, traces and events. It separates compute from storage, keeping indexes on S3-compatible object storage, so stateless searchers can scale out and retention costs a fraction of an Elasticsearch hot tier. It offers an Elasticsearch-compatible query API, native Jaeger and OpenTelemetry endpoints, and Kafka/Kinesis/Pulsar ingestion. Datadog acquired Quickwit in early 2025 and relicensed it from AGPL to Apache-2.0; development continues in the open with the 0.9 line.

pricing.notes: Free and open source; there is no vendor-managed Quickwit service.

scale.notes: Stateless indexers and searchers over object storage; Binance runs a 100 PB log service ingesting about 1.6 PB per day.

strengths: Indexes live on object storage, so long retention is cheap
Stateless searchers scale independently of ingest
Native OpenTelemetry and Jaeger endpoints for traces and logs
Elasticsearch-compatible search API works with Grafana and existing tools
weaknesses: Optimised for append-only data; updates and deletes are limited
Object-storage latency makes it slower than RAM-heavy engines for interactive app search
Future roadmap depends on Datadog's priorities
useCases: Log search and retention at large scale
Cheap replacement for Elasticsearch hot-warm logging clusters
notIdealFor: E-commerce or app search with frequent updates
